findings.title: Brittle co-location assumption embedded in core wire types
findings.location: Section 0. Scope, Deployment constraint — co-location and Section 7.1 ScreenshotResult
findings.evidence: This constraint is load-bearing: `ScreenshotResult` (Section 7.1) transmits file paths rather than image bytes. Remote deployment is out of scope for this version.
findings.problem: The wire contract itself (file paths + shared directory) hard-codes a Windows co-location assumption that cannot be relaxed without breaking every consumer of ScreenshotResult, despite the claim that only deployment is out of scope.
findings.why_it_matters: Creates permanent architectural lock-in; any future remote, containerized, or cross-machine use immediately invalidates the protocol, contradicting the 'all other specs reference types defined here and add nothing' claim.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace path transmission with byte payload or content-addressable reference usable for both local and remote cases; mark current design as explicitly deprecated for v2.

findings.title: Version-mismatch error message uses version-specific format
findings.location: Section 10. Protocol Versioning and Section 5 ClientProtocolErrorMessage definition
findings.evidence: Mismatch → orchestrator sends `ClientProtocolErrorMessage(ErrorCode: VersionMismatch)` with both versions populated, then closes the WebSocket. Exact string match required.
findings.problem: If the two sides have divergent polymorphic registrations, record layouts, or enum values, the error message serialized under one version cannot be deserialized by the other, preventing the very diagnostic the handshake intends.
findings.why_it_matters: Handshake becomes unusable for the incompatible changes it was designed to catch; results in raw WebSocket closure with no error details, violating the stated goal of boundary validation rules.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a minimal, stable plain-JSON error format outside the polymorphic families that both sides can always parse, or send error as text frame before close.

findings.title: Hash canonicalization incorrectly shifts ordering burden to producers
findings.location: Section 13. Hash Canonicalization, Array ordering rules for hashed types
findings.evidence: Producers MUST emit arrays in canonical order... FeatureNode lists ordered by FeatureId... FeatureParameter lists ordered by Name... SelectionRef lists (Persistent first then Sketch)... Property-based tests assert logical equality implies hash equality.
findings.problem: Requiring every producer (orchestrator, future SPEC-05 agents, SPEC-06 UI) to know and implement these exact sort orders duplicates logic that belongs inside HashCanonicalizer.ComputeFeatureTreeHash.
findings.why_it_matters: Contradicts the 'single source of truth' philosophy asserted in Section 11 for tool names; multiplies surface for divergence, makes property tests a band-aid rather than prevention, and inflates cognitive load for every future change.
findings.proposed_fix: Move sorting inside the canonicalizer (sort by defined keys before hashing); remove producer MUST rules and update property tests to only verify logical equivalence after normalization.

findings.title: AddinSessionId generation and validation underspecified for adversarial conditions
findings.location: Section 9. AddinSessionId and Epoch (including GenerateAddinSessionId code) and Section 14. Validation
findings.evidence: generated by the add-in deterministically from (machineGuid, swProcessId, loadTimestamp)... return Convert.ToHexString(hash)[..32]... Any non-AddinReadyMessage with an AddinSessionId other than the current epoch is rejected with StaleEpoch. No validator mentioned for session ID format.
findings.problem: No definition of GetMachineGuid behavior, no collision analysis for rapid restarts or clock skew, no format/length validator in Validation/Validators, and no handling for maliciously crafted colliding or malformed session IDs.
findings.why_it_matters: Epoch mechanism becomes single point of failure under process forking, VM snapshot restore, or deliberate attack; downstream SPEC-03 state machine will reject legitimate messages with no recovery path beyond full reconnect.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify entropy source, minimum collision probability, add strict regex/length validator for 32 lowercase hex, and define recovery behavior when epoch collisions are detected.

findings.title: Over-specified CI tests create brittle dependency on perfect test environment
findings.location: Section 15. Test Requirements (Build-Breaking), specifically HashCanonicalization_PropertyTests (FsCheck): 1000 randomized trees, ValidationSchemaSyncTests, and ArchitectureTests
findings.evidence: Failure of any of these fails CI... FsCheck: 1000 randomly shaped FeatureNode trees... Advisory tests run in separate CI step with continue-on-error: true so they report without blocking.
findings.problem: Mandating 1000 randomized cases plus build-breaking tests for naming, completeness, schema sync, and architecture in every PR creates non-deterministic CI failures dependent on FsCheck seed, machine performance, and exact reflection behavior.
findings.why_it_matters: Turns protocol changes into high-friction events for all dependent specs (SPEC-02 through SPEC-06); complexity inflation that does not scale beyond hackathon without becoming maintenance tax.
findings.proposed_fix: Reduce property tests to 100 iterations, move advisory schema/architecture checks to nightly-only, and document that test count itself is subject to revision before v1.0.
